input: Simulate a build pipeline: 1) Check that /src/main.c and /src/utils.c exist, 2) 'Compile' each .c file by copying it to /build/ with a .o extension and prepending '// compiled', 3) 'Link' by concatenating all .o files into /build/program with a '// linked' header, 4) 'Package' by creating a tar.gz of /build/ at /dist/release.tar.gz. Print status for each stage. If any stage fails, stop and report the error.

transcript.final_response:
Build pipeline completed successfully:

- Check: OK
- Compile: OK
- Link: OK
- Package: OK — `/dist/release.tar.gz`
tool_calls:
set -e
stage="Check"
fail() { code=$?; printf 'ERROR: %s stage failed (exit %s)\n' "$stage" "$code"; exit "$code"; }
trap fail ERR
printf 'Checking inputs...\n'
test -f /src/main.c
test -f /src/utils.c
printf 'Check: OK\n'
stage="Compile"
mkdir -p /build
for file in /src/main.c /src/utils.c; do
  name=$(basename "$file" .c)
  { printf '// compiled\n'; cat "$file"; } > "/build/$name.o"
done
printf 'Compile: OK\n'
stage="Link"
{ printf '// linked\n'; cat /build/*.o; } > /build/program
printf 'Link: OK\n'
stage="Package"
mkdir -p /dist
tar -czf /dist/release.tar.gz -C /build .
printf 'Package: OK (/dist/release.tar.gz)\n'
